key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current influence penetration, molten-pool flow, and arc stability in distinct ways.
engineering_relevance: These relationships can guide parameter selection for welding low-expansion Invar components used in aerospace composite molds.
method: High-speed photography of pool evolution and arc behavior
Comparison across laser power, welding speed, and current ranges
evidence_signal: Within 5–6 kW, higher power increased penetration and arc deflection tendency; within 0.5–0.8 m/min, higher speed reduced penetration and width; within 150–170 A, higher current widened the weld and improved arc stability.
watch_item: The reported trends are limited to the studied parameter ranges; the abstract provides no quantitative simulation-validation errors.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
